How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of October 1, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to received and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2024-2025 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for September 2024.

  D. FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2024,
  FOR THE GENERAL FUND AND MISSION PLAYHOUSE FUND

  This report provides a Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget update for the City’s
  general fund and Mission Playhouse fund as of September 30, 2024. The budget
  update incorporates the actual revenue received and expenditures that have
  occurred through September 30, 2024, and projects the financial results for the
  year ending on June 30, 2025. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 YEAR-END APPROPRIATION ADJUSTMENTS
  [RESOLUTION NO. 24-63]

  As the City’s Fiscal Year 2023-2024 financial books are being closed, it becomes
  necessary to make budget adjustments prior to the forthcoming audit. These
  adjustments are necessary to allocate additional funds to general fund
  departments or other funds that have surpassed their initially allocated or

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  3
   amended budgets. This report seeks the approval of the City Council for these
  budget adjustments, which may involve transferring appropriations between
  general fund departments or appropriating funds to a fund that has exceeded
  its budget appropriations. General fund departments and funds that exceed
  approved budgets are disclosed in the audited financial statements.
  Additionally, this report provides detailed explanations for each of the
  proposed adjustments. Budgeted funds will be adjusted to bring all general
  fund departments and City funds within approved budgets.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-63 approving
  proposed amendments to the annual budget for fiscal year 2023-2024.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 24-53 AMENDING RESOLUTION NO. 14-39, ARTICLE 8.,
  DISPATCHER TRAINING BONUS

  As the San Gabriel Police Department continues to grow in size and embrace
  new technology to better serve the community, training new employees is a
  vital step in their development and, more importantly, in the mission of the
  organization. To fulfill the training needs of new employees and to have
  tenured Department employees conduct the training, it is equitable that all
  Department employees who train to be fairly compensated for this additional
  responsibility, which is not part of their current job classification or daily
  responsibilities. The fiscal impact on the San Gabriel Police Department general
  fund is limited, as the training pay is only applied to full-time employees who
  are actively training a probationary coworker. The bonus is capped at 5% of the
  employee’s base salary. Training periods regularly last between four and six
  months. The cost associated with this amendment is estimated to be $3,600 for
  the remainder of the fiscal year. Funds are available in the Department budget
  to absorb this additional cost.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-53, amending
  Resolution No. 14-39, Article 8, to include the job classifications of Dispatcher,

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  4
   Property and Evidence Technician and Records Specialist to change the title for
  Article 8.

  G. PURCHASE OF AIR RESPIRATORS FROM MALLORY SAFETY AND SUPPLY
  UNDER 2022 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT PROGRAM IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $51,390.06

  The San Gabriel Police Department was awarded a grant from the 2022 State
  Homeland Security Program (SHSP) in the amount of $51,363 dedicated to the
  procurement of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS). Due to an urgent need and
  priority to replace the current aging air respirators, staff is seeking to utilize this
  funding towards the purchase of sixty-five air respirators to enhance the safety
  of our Police Officers. The initial outlay of $51,363 for the air respirators will be
  fully funded by the 2022 SHSP grant award. The remaining balance of $27.06
  will come out of the Department’s budget. The deadline to use these funds is
  February 2025 and will be reimbursed within 120 days of the submission of a
  reimbursement request.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to purchase
  65 air respirators equipment using the allocated State Homeland Security
  Program grant funding.

  H. ORDINANCE NO. 710: AMENDING THE VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC
  PLAN RELATING TO GROUND FLOOR OFFICE USE AND ESTABLISHING
  MINIMUM DENSITIES (SPA24-001) – SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 710 was introduced by a 5-0 vote of the City Council at the
  October 1, 2024, City Council meeting. Adoption of Ordinance No. 710 would
  amend the Valley Boulevard Specific Plan relating to ground floor office use
  and establish minimum densities intended to implement the goals and
  programs identified in the 2021-2029 Housing Element. The Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025 adopted budget includes the cost for required legal publication (Account
  No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of
  the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). An Initial Study / Negative Declaration (IS/ND) was prepared

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  5
   for the 2021-2029 Housing Element, as required by CEQA, Public Resources Code
  (PRC) Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA Guidelines, and the City of San Gabriel
  Local Guidelines for Implementing CEQA. The IS/ND considered the policies and
  programs outlined in the Housing Element. The Housing Element establishes the
  objectives, policies, and programs to assist the City in achieving state-mandated
  housing goals. No formal land use changes or physical development would
  require separate environmental evaluation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  710 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case No. SPA24-001, Amending the Valley
  Boulevard Specific Plan Relating to ground floor office use and establish
  minimum densities intended to implement the goals and programs identified
  in the 2021-2029 Housing Element.”

  I. RESOLUTION NO. 24-55 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 800 BLOCK OF COMMERCIAL AVENUE

  This item requests a temporary street closure for Ogopogo Brewing’s 6 th
  Anniversary Celebration on Saturday, October 26, 2024, on the 800 block of
  Commercial Avenue from South Gladys Avenue to the end of the cul-de-sac.
  There is no fiscal impact to the budget for this event. Regularly scheduled staff
  time will be used for this event.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-55 authorizing
  a temporary street closure on the 800 block of Commercial Avenue from South
  Gladys Avenue to the end of the cul-de-sac from 12:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. on
  Saturday, October 26, 2024.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 405 SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE
  PLANNING CASE NO: GPA24-001, ZC24-002, DENSITY BONUS AND
  STREET VACATION (GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT, ZONE CHANGE)
  APPLICANT: THE RELATED COMPANIES OF CALIFORNIA, LIMITED
  LIABILITY COMPANY [ORDINANCE NO. 714]

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  6
   The subject request is a General Plan Amendment, Zone Change, Density
  Bonus, and Street Vacation to allow for the development of a one hundred
  percent affordable senior housing development at 405 South Del Mar Avenue.
  The property is zoned M-1 (Light Manufacturing) and has a General Plan Use
  Designation of Light Industrial. The project site is 70,307 square feet (1.6 acres)
  in size, including a 12-foot street vacation totaling 11,392 square feet, and is
  currently vacant. The Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Adopted Budget includes the cost
  for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance, if adopted by
  the City Council.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project was
  reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
  This project is exempt from the requirements of CEQA, per Guideline Section
  21080.40 (Definitions; affordable housing projects and rezoning exemption).
  Technical studies, including traffic, acoustic, and a Phase I and Phase II
  environmental site assessment were prepared by the applicant team and
  submitted to the City and Department of Toxic Substances Control for review.

  On July 23, 2024, the City submitted letters requesting tribal consultation with
  the associated tribal representatives by August 22, 2024. The City received a
  request for consultation from the Gabrielino Band of Mission Indians – Kizh
  Nation. Consultation concluded on September 3, 2024. The project site has a
  moderate sensitivity for buried Native American archaeological deposits and
  cultural materials. Therefore, the potential to tribal cultural resources on-site is
  moderate. Given the moderate sensitivity of the project site, even with the
  previous disturbance, there could still be a moderate likelihood of encountering
  tribal cultural resources during project construction. The Native American Historic
  Resource Act; Archaeological, Paleontological, and Historic Sites; Native
  American Historical, Cultural, and Sacred Sites (Public Resources Code Section
  5097-5097.994) specifies the procedures to be followed in the event of unexpected
  discovery of human remains on nonfederal public lands. Adherence to existing
  State regulations and the procedures in the City’s Historic Preservation and
  Cultural Resources Ordinance (SGMC Section 153.630); would ensure that
  potential impacts on tribal cultural resources would be reduced to less than
  significant levels.

  Recommended Action:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the General Plan Amendment, Zone Change, Density Bonus, and
  Street Vacation applications. Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  7
   1 . Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 714;

  2 . Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 714 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING PLANNING CASE NUMBERS
  GPA24-001, ZC24-002, DENSITY BONUS, STREET VACATION TO
  ALLOW FOR AN ONE HUNDRED PERCENT AFFORDABLE SENIOR
  HOUSING DEVELOPMENT AT 405 SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE,
  SUBJECT TO CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second
  reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City
  Council meeting. The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days
  after adoption.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  FARM HABITS FOR THE CERTIFIED FARMER’S MARKET AND BUDGET
  APPROPRIATION OF AN ADDITIONAL $4,000 FOR MARKETING AND
  EQUIPMENT [RESOLUTION NO. 24-62]

  In late April, the City and Supporting Arms launched the San Gabriel Farmer’s
  Market. Despite many efforts, the Farmer’s Market was not able to consistently
  retain vendors, attendance to the event decreased. At the August 20, 2024, City
  Council meeting, the City Council directed staff to return with an agreement to
  onboard Farm Habits as the new farmer’s market operator. The Council
  determined that the closure of Mission Drive adjacent to Blossom Market Food
  Hall would be the best location to relaunch the market and to host the market
  on Saturday mornings. At the September 17, 2024, City Council meeting, the
  Couuncil continued the item to allow time for the owner of Farm Habits to
  attend the meeting. The intent of this report is to present the City Council with
  the draft agreement with Farm Habits for consideration and approval and to
  discuss the next steps toward relaunching the farmer’s market. $25,000 would
  be needed to cover equipment rental costs as well as advertising and marketing
  efforts for fiscal year 2024-2025. The fiscal year 2024-2025 includes $21,000 for
  the farmer’s market special event. To meet the staff recommended $25,000
  budget for the event, and additional $4,000 will need to be appropriated to the
  fiscal year 2024-2025 budget for this special event. The fee waiver, if approved,
  would reduce the potential revenue by $3,237.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  8
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Review and authorize the Professional Services Agreement with Farm
  Habits and authorize the City Manager to execute it;
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 24-62 for the appropriation of funds; and
  3. Approve a fee waiver of all business license fees and taxes for the
  farmer’s market.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION AND DISCUSSION ON ESTABLISHING A SISTER CITY
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND HUALIEN COUNTY, TAIWAN
  REPUBLIC OF CHINA

  In January 2024, the City Council adopted an official City policy to govern how
  future Sister City requests are handled. In June 2024, the City Council approved
  a Sister City Agreement with the Banqiao District of New Taipei City in Taiwan
  Republic of China (R.O.C.). Since that time, Hualien County, Taiwan R.O.C. has
  shown interest in forming a Sister City with San Gabriel and would like to move
  forward with drafting a formal agreement.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as it has no reasonable
  potential for significantly impacting the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council Discuss and provide direction on
  establishing a Sister City Program with Hualien County, Taiwan R.O.C. to
  promote cultural diversity. Should the City Council decide to form a Sister City
  partnership, a draft agreement has been attached to the report for
  consideration.

  B. POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE 2024

  This item provides an update on Police Department operations, goals,
  challenges, and objectives.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2024  9
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  This is a presentation item only; no action is required.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 19, 2024
  at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION AND DISCUSSION ON ESTABLISHING A SISTER CITY
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND HUALIEN COUNTY, TAIWAN
  REPUBLIC OF CHINA

I  City Manager Lazzaretto and Mayor Wu made the presentation.
  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included having diversity of countries for sister city relationships; a
  focus on relationships rather than countries; willingness of both parties to partner;
  an already established connection with Hualien County; and the potential tourism
  benefit for San Gabriel.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Council Member Ding,
  to approve the Sister City agreement with Hualien County, Taiwan Republic of
  China.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE
